# Prepare Survey Data

## L2 variables

```{r}
## =====================================================================
## Per-scale validation via CFAstats() + composite descriptives
## Loops your CFAstats() wrapper over every scale, then computes the
## scale-score mean_<short> / SD_<short> objects (e.g. mean_cmq, SD_cmq).
##
## Requires in scope:
##   - stringr, psych, lavaan, semPlot, moments, ggplot2/dplyr/tidyr/forcats
##   - your helpers: CFAstats(), getDescriptivesSurvey(), model_lavaan(),
##     dimensionalityTest(), explorativeFactorAnalysis()
##   - the data frame `ques_study`
## =====================================================================

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Scale definitions
##    - list name   = suffix for mean_<name> / SD_<name>
##    - labelLatent = passed to CFAstats(); also used as the lavaan latent
##                    variable name, so it MUST be a valid identifier
##                    (no spaces, no "-"). CFAstats strips "-" from the
##                    *item* names/regex itself, so keep "-" in regEx.
##    - regEx       = column selector (matches the ORIGINAL column names)
##    The ^ anchor stops "^utopianism" from catching "anti_utopianism".
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
scaleConfig <- list(
  activism   = list(labelLatent = "ARIS_Activism",               regEx = "^aris_scale-ais"),
  radicalism = list(labelLatent = "ARIS_Radicalism",             regEx = "^aris_scale-ris"),
  utop       = list(labelLatent = "Utopianism",                  regEx = "^utopianism_scale-utop"),
  antiutop   = list(labelLatent = "AntiUtopianism",              regEx = "^anti_utopianism_scale-antiutop"),
  nfc        = list(labelLatent = "NeedForChaos",                regEx = "^nfc_scale-nfc"),
  sjs        = list(labelLatent = "SystemJustification",         regEx = "^sjs_scale-sjs"),
  swls       = list(labelLatent = "SatisfactionWithLife",        regEx = "^swls_scale-swls"),
  brs        = list(labelLatent = "BriefResilience",             regEx = "^brs_scale-brs"),
  prds       = list(labelLatent = "PersonalRelativeDeprivation", regEx = "^prds_scale-prds"),
  cmq        = list(labelLatent = "ConspiracyMentality",         regEx = "^cmq_scale-cmq")
)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1b. Reverse-code the reverse-keyed (…r) items  --  RUN ONCE
##     Formula (as requested): reversed = max(item) - item, using each
##     item's own (empirical) maximum.
##     Applied to the global ques_study BEFORE CFAstats() and the
##     composites, so EFA/CFA loadings come out positive and the scale
##     means are correct.
##     Guarded against accidental re-running (re-flipping would corrupt
##     the values) -- reload ques_study fresh if you need to redo it.
##     Note: max(item) - item puts the reversed items on a 0..(max-min)
##     range. To keep them on the original min..max scale instead, use
##     (min(item) + max(item)) - item.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
revCols <- c("sjs_scale-sjs3r", "sjs_scale-sjs7r",
             "brs_scale-brs2r", "brs_scale-brs4r", "brs_scale-brs6r",
             "prds_scale-prds2r", "prds_scale-prds4r")

if (!exists("reverseCodingDone") || !isTRUE(reverseCodingDone)) {
  for (col in revCols) {
    ques_study_wide[[col]] <- max(ques_study_wide[[col]], na.rm = TRUE) - ques_study_wide[[col]]
  }
  reverseCodingDone <- TRUE
  message("Reverse-coded (max - item): ", paste(revCols, collapse = ", "))
} else {
  message("Reverse coding already applied; skipping. Reload ques_study_wide to redo.")
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Run CFAstats() for every scale
##    Toggle the components once here; they apply to all scales.
##    NB: CFAstats() runs the EFA as a fixed 1-factor solution and the
##        CFA as a 1-factor (unidimensional) lavaan model.
##        Mplus is OFF (needs Mplus installed; latent name must be <=8
##        chars for Mplus -- shorten labelLatent above if you enable it).
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
opt_showPlots       <- TRUE   # cor.plot + getDescriptivesSurvey()
opt_computeEFA      <- TRUE   # dimensionalityTest() + 1-factor EFA
opt_computeCFA      <- TRUE   # lavaan 1-factor CFA (MLR) + semPaths + MIs
opt_computeCFAMplus <- FALSE  # Mplus CFA + McDonald's omega

cfaResults <- list()
for (short in names(scaleConfig)) {
  cfg <- scaleConfig[[short]]
  cat("\n\n===================== ", cfg$labelLatent, " =====================\n")

  cfaResults[[short]] <- CFAstats(
    dataset         = ques_study_wide,
    regularExp      = cfg$regEx,
    labelLatent     = cfg$labelLatent,
    showPlots       = opt_showPlots,
    computeEFA      = opt_computeEFA,
    computeCFA      = opt_computeCFA,
    computeCFAMplus = opt_computeCFAMplus
  )
}
## inspect later, e.g.:
##   cfaResults$cmq$EFA[[1]]$loadings
##   cfaResults$cmq$cronbachAlpha$total$raw_alpha
##   summary(cfaResults$cmq$CFA, fit.measures = TRUE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Per-participant scale scores -> bind as new columns to ques_study_wide
##    For every scale and every participant (row), ONE value each:
##      mean_<short> = row mean across the scale's items   (na.rm = TRUE)
##      sd_<short>   = row SD   across the scale's items    (na.rm = TRUE)
##    sd_<short> captures within-person spread across that scale's items.
##    Reverse coding (step 1b) is already applied to ques_study_wide, so the
##    items are correctly oriented here.
##    (For large data, apply(.,1,sd) can be replaced by matrixStats::rowSds.)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
for (short in names(scaleConfig)) {
  cfg   <- scaleConfig[[short]]
  sel   <- str_detect(colnames(ques_study_wide), cfg$regEx)
  items <- as.matrix(ques_study_wide[, sel])

  ques_study_wide[[paste0("mean_", short)]] <- rowMeans(items, na.rm = TRUE)
  ques_study_wide[[paste0("sd_",   short)]] <- apply(items, 1L, sd, na.rm = TRUE)
}

## peek at the new columns
head(ques_study_wide[, grep("^(mean|sd)_", colnames(ques_study_wide)), drop = FALSE])

## OPTIONAL: sample-level summary (mean & SD ACROSS participants of each
## scale's mean score) -- the earlier mean_<short>/SD_<short> table.
descriptives <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(scaleConfig), function(short) {
  sc <- ques_study_wide[[paste0("mean_", short)]]
  data.frame(scale   = scaleConfig[[short]]$labelLatent,
             mean    = mean(sc, na.rm = TRUE),
             sd      = sd(sc,   na.rm = TRUE),
             n_items = sum(str_detect(colnames(ques_study_wide),
                                      scaleConfig[[short]]$regEx)))
}))
descriptives
```


```{r}
########################################
# correlation plot of all scale means
########################################
corPlotMeans <- function(dataset, pattern = "^mean_", main = "Scale means") {
  sel <- stringr::str_detect(colnames(dataset), pattern)
  m   <- dataset[, sel, drop = FALSE]
  colnames(m) <- sub(pattern, "", colnames(m))      # drop "mean_" for cleaner labels
  tmp_cor <- cor(m, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  psych::cor.plot(r = tmp_cor, upper = FALSE, xlas = 2, main = main)
  invisible(tmp_cor)                                # returns the matrix too
}

corPlotMeans(ques_study_wide)
```



## L1 variables


```{r}
## =====================================================================
## Within-vignettes analysis (long -> per-row composites -> wide EFA)
## Data: ques_study_within_vignettes
##   one row per participant x vignette; 7 vignettes (condition_FutureSociety)
##   per PROLIFIC_PID. No reverse coding needed.
## Requires: stringr, psych, dplyr, tidyr
##   (+ your helpers CFAstats(), dimensionalityTest(),
##      explorativeFactorAnalysis() if you run the optional item-level part)
## =====================================================================


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 0. Items are stored as <chr> -> convert to numeric
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
itemCols <- c("pe1", "pe2", "pe3", "pe4",
              "att_ideal", "att_beneficial", "att_utopian",
              "att_desirable", "att_innovative", "att_live_in")

ques_study_within_vignettes[itemCols] <-
  lapply(ques_study_within_vignettes[itemCols], as.numeric)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Scale definitions (no reverse items here)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
scaleConfigWithin <- list(
  pe  = list(labelLatent = "PE",  regEx = "^pe[0-9]+$"),  # pe1..pe4
  att = list(labelLatent = "ATT", regEx = "^att_")        # the 6 att_* items
)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. (OPTIONAL) item-level validation via CFAstats(), same as before.
##    pe/att items are ordered Likert, so polychoric (the helper's
##    non-"Overall" path) is appropriate here.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# cfaResultsWithin <- list()
# for (short in names(scaleConfigWithin)) {
#   cfg <- scaleConfigWithin[[short]]
#   cat("\n\n===================== ", cfg$labelLatent, " =====================\n")
#   cfaResultsWithin[[short]] <- CFAstats(
#     dataset = as.data.frame(ques_study_within_vignettes),
#     regularExp = cfg$regEx, labelLatent = cfg$labelLatent,
#     showPlots = TRUE, computeEFA = TRUE, computeCFA = TRUE, computeCFAMplus = FALSE)
# }

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Per-participant-per-vignette composites -> bind to the long data
##    mean_<short> = row mean across the scale's items   (na.rm = TRUE)
##    sd_<short>   = row SD   across the scale's items    (na.rm = TRUE)
##    -> one value per row (participant x vignette).
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
for (short in names(scaleConfigWithin)) {
  cfg   <- scaleConfigWithin[[short]]
  sel   <- str_detect(colnames(ques_study_within_vignettes), cfg$regEx)
  items <- as.matrix(ques_study_within_vignettes[, sel])

  ques_study_within_vignettes[[paste0("mean_", short)]] <- rowMeans(items, na.rm = TRUE)
  ques_study_within_vignettes[[paste0("sd_",   short)]] <- apply(items, 1L, sd, na.rm = TRUE)
}

head(ques_study_within_vignettes[, grep("^(mean|sd)_(pe|att)$",
                                         colnames(ques_study_within_vignettes)),
                                  drop = FALSE])

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Reshape to WIDE: one row per PROLIFIC_PID, one column per society.
##    Cell = that participant's composite score for that society.
##    values_fn guards against a participant seeing a society >1 time.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
makeWide <- function(data, valueCol,
                     idCol  = "PROLIFIC_PID",
                     keyCol = "condition_FutureSociety") {
  data %>%
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(idCol, keyCol, valueCol))) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(
      id_cols     = dplyr::all_of(idCol),
      names_from  = dplyr::all_of(keyCol),
      values_from = dplyr::all_of(valueCol),
      values_fn   = function(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Correlation plot + parallel analysis + EFA on the wide matrix.
##    Composites are continuous, so use Pearson (not polychoric).
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
corEFAwide <- function(wide, idCol = "PROLIFIC_PID", label = "wide") {
  m <- as.data.frame(wide[, setdiff(colnames(wide), idCol), drop = FALSE])

  ## correlation heat-map across the 7 societies
  tmp_cor <- cor(m, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  psych::cor.plot(r = tmp_cor, upper = FALSE, xlas = 2, main = label)

  ## parallel analysis -> suggested number of factors
  pa <- psych::fa.parallel(m, fm = "minres", fa = "both", main = label, cor = "cor")
  nf <- max(1, pa$nfact)

  ## EFA
  efa <- psych::fa(r = tmp_cor, nfactors = nf,
                   rotate = if (nf > 1) "promax" else "none",
                   n.obs = nrow(m))
  cat("\n", label, " - EFA loadings (", nf, " factor(s)):\n", sep = "")
  print(efa$loadings)

  list(cor = tmp_cor, parallel = pa, nfact = nf, efa = efa)
}

## build wide data + run, for each composite
wide_pe  <- makeWide(ques_study_within_vignettes, "mean_pe")
wide_att <- makeWide(ques_study_within_vignettes, "mean_att")

res_pe_wide  <- corEFAwide(wide_pe,  label = "PE across societies")
res_att_wide <- corEFAwide(wide_att, label = "ATT across societies")

## inspect later, e.g. res_att_wide$efa$loadings ; res_att_wide$nfact
```

# Get Data for Hypothesis

## H1

```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 0. Variable groups to keep
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
sampleVars <- c("age", "gender", "education", "employment_status", "employment_is_employed",
                "lrscale", "rlgdgr")                       # sample description
rankVars   <- grep("^rank_", colnames(ques_study_wide), value = TRUE)  # ranking task
 
## Governance grouping (EDIT here if a prototype belongs elsewhere).
## self-governed = self-determined societal change; everything else
## (religious, aicentered, lawBased, futurist) = externally determined.
self_governed_conditions <- c("moderngreen", "primitivist", "anarchic") # all others are non-self governed
 
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Build the H1 subset (long; keeps ranking + sample descriptors)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
data_H1 <- ques_study_within_vignettes %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    self_externally_governed = factor(
      ifelse(condition_FutureSociety %in% self_governed_conditions,
             "self_governed", "externally_governed"),
      levels = c("externally_governed", "self_governed"))   # external = reference
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(ID, PROLIFIC_PID, condition_FutureSociety, vignette_id,
                self_externally_governed,
                mean_pe, sd_pe, att_live_in, mean_att, sd_att) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    dplyr::select(ques_study_wide,
                  dplyr::all_of(c("PROLIFIC_PID", sampleVars, rankVars))),
    by = "PROLIFIC_PID")
 
## sanity: which prototypes landed in each bucket
table(data_H1$condition_FutureSociety, data_H1$self_externally_governed)
 
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Describe the sample (participant level: one row per person)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
sample_desc <- ques_study_wide %>%
  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c("PROLIFIC_PID", sampleVars))) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()
psych::describe(sample_desc[, c("age", "lrscale", "rlgdgr")])
lapply(sample_desc[, c("gender", "education", "employment_status")], table)
 
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Test H1 (within-person: random intercept per participant)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## group means
data_H1 %>%
  dplyr::group_by(self_externally_governed) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(M_pe   = mean(mean_pe,     na.rm = TRUE),
                   SD_pe  = sd(mean_pe,       na.rm = TRUE),
                   M_live = mean(att_live_in, na.rm = TRUE),
                   SD_live= sd(att_live_in,   na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
 
## participative efficacy
m_pe   <- lmer(mean_pe     ~ self_externally_governed + (1 | PROLIFIC_PID), data = data_H1)
## "want to live in" evaluation
m_live <- lmer(att_live_in ~ self_externally_governed + (1 | PROLIFIC_PID), data = data_H1)
summary(m_pe)
summary(m_live)
 
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Export the H1 subset: SPSS (.sav), Excel (.xlsx), R (.rds)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
exportDataset <- function(df, base, dir = ".") {
  if (!dir.exists(dir)) dir.create(dir, recursive = TRUE)
  clean <- df; names(clean) <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", names(clean))  # SPSS/Excel-safe names
  haven::write_sav(clean, file.path(dir, paste0(base, ".sav")))          # factors -> labelled
  xl <- clean; f <- vapply(xl, is.factor, logical(1))
  xl[f] <- lapply(xl[f], as.character)                                   # writexl wants atomic cols
  writexl::write_xlsx(xl, file.path(dir, paste0(base, ".xlsx")))
  saveRDS(df, file.path(dir, paste0(base, ".rds")))                      # keeps original names/types
  invisible(NULL)
}
 
exportDataset(data_H1, "data_H1", OUTPUT_QUESTIONNAIRE_PIA_DIR)
```

### plots H1

```{r}
## =====================================================================
## Plot H1: participative efficacy & "want to live in" by governance group
## =====================================================================
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## A) Descriptive plot straight from the group means (mean +/- 95% CI)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
plot_dat <- data_H1 %>%
  dplyr::group_by(self_externally_governed) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    M_pe   = mean(mean_pe,     na.rm = TRUE),
    SE_pe  = sd(mean_pe,       na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(mean_pe))),
    M_live = mean(att_live_in, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE_live= sd(att_live_in,   na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(att_live_in))),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-self_externally_governed,
                      names_to = c(".value", "outcome"), names_sep = "_") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    outcome = factor(outcome, levels = c("pe", "live"),
                     labels = c("Participative efficacy", "Want to live in")),
    lo = M - 1.96 * SE, hi = M + 1.96 * SE)

ggplot(plot_dat, aes(self_externally_governed, M, fill = self_externally_governed)) +
  geom_col(width = .6) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = .15) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", M)), vjust = -0.6, size = 3.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ outcome, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(externally_governed = "#9aa6b2",
                               self_governed        = "#3f7cac")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean (\u00B1 95% CI)",
       title = "H1: prototype agency",
       subtitle = "Self- vs externally-governed future societies") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## B) Model-based plot from the mixed models (marginal means + 95% CI)
##    Matches the lmer tests; install.packages("emmeans") if needed.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
library(emmeans)

emm <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(emmeans(m_pe,   ~ self_externally_governed)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(outcome = "Participative efficacy"),
  as.data.frame(emmeans(m_live, ~ self_externally_governed)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(outcome = "Want to live in")
)

## emmeans names the CI columns lower.CL/upper.CL (t-based) OR
## asymp.LCL/asymp.UCL (z-based, as with lmer). Normalise to lo/hi.
emm$lo <- if ("lower.CL" %in% names(emm)) emm$lower.CL else emm$asymp.LCL
emm$hi <- if ("upper.CL" %in% names(emm)) emm$upper.CL else emm$asymp.UCL

ggplot(emm, aes(self_externally_governed, emmean, colour = self_externally_governed)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = .15) +
  facet_wrap(~ outcome, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(externally_governed = "#9aa6b2",
                                 self_governed        = "#3f7cac")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Estimated marginal mean (\u00B1 95% CI)",
       title = "H1: model-estimated means") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## C) Grouped barplot for the SEVEN single conditions (mean +/- 95% CI),
##    coloured by governance bucket, faceted by outcome.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
cond_dat <- data_H1 %>%
  dplyr::group_by(condition_FutureSociety, self_externally_governed) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    M_pe   = mean(mean_pe,     na.rm = TRUE),
    SE_pe  = sd(mean_pe,       na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(mean_pe))),
    M_live = mean(att_live_in, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE_live= sd(att_live_in,   na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(att_live_in))),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(M_pe, SE_pe, M_live, SE_live),
                      names_to = c(".value", "outcome"), names_sep = "_") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    outcome = factor(outcome, levels = c("pe", "live"),
                     labels = c("Participative efficacy", "Want to live in")),
    lo = M - 1.96 * SE, hi = M + 1.96 * SE)

ggplot(cond_dat,
       aes(x = reorder(condition_FutureSociety, M), y = M,
           fill = self_externally_governed)) +
  geom_col(width = .7) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = .2) +
  facet_wrap(~ outcome, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(externally_governed = "#9aa6b2",
                               self_governed        = "#3f7cac"),
                    name = "Governance") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean (\u00B1 95% CI)",
       title = "H1: per-condition means",
       subtitle = "Seven future-society prototypes, coloured by governance bucket") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "top")
```


## H2




```{r}
## =====================================================================
## H2 setup: pull each participant's preferred-society row(s)
## Ranking (ques_study_wide, rank_* columns) -> most preferred society
## per participant -> extract that participant's matching row from the
## long within-vignettes data (pe = participative efficacy, att = eval.,
## plus any BI / AIS-adapted columns it contains).
## Requires: stringr, dplyr, tidyr
## =====================================================================

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## ASSUMPTIONS -- check these against your codebook
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
idCol <- "PROLIFIC_PID"   # common key in BOTH datasets; switch to "ID" if needed

## rank value 1 == MOST preferred (L1), 2 == second (L2), ... 7 == least.
## (If 7 is most preferred in your coding, flip with: rank <- 8 - rank.)

## map rank_* suffixes -> condition_FutureSociety labels in the long data.
## LEFT = suffix after "rank_"  ;  RIGHT = value in condition_FutureSociety.
society_map <- c(
  religious      = "religious",
  ai_centered    = "aicentered",
  primitivist    = "primitivist",
  institutional  = "lawBased",
  moral_anarchic = "anarchic",
  futurist       = "futurist",
  modern_green   = "moderngreen"
)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## Function: rows from the long data for each participant's n-th
## preferred society (level = 1 -> L1 most preferred, 2 -> L2, ...).
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
extractPreferredRows <- function(level     = 1,
                                 wide      = ques_study_wide,
                                 long      = ques_study_within_vignettes,
                                 id        = idCol,
                                 societyMap = society_map) {

  rankCols <- stringr::str_subset(colnames(wide), "^rank")

  pref <- wide %>%
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(id, rankCols))) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::all_of(rankCols),
                        names_to = "society_rankvar", values_to = "rank") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      society_rank            = sub("^rank_", "", society_rankvar),
      condition_FutureSociety = unname(societyMap[society_rank])
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(rank == level) %>%                 # rank == 1 -> L1, == 2 -> L2
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(id), condition_FutureSociety, rank) %>%
    dplyr::rename(pref_rank = rank)

  ## warn if any society_rank wasn't mapped
  unmapped <- setdiff(sub("^rank_", "", rankCols), names(societyMap))
  if (length(unmapped)) warning("Unmapped rank suffixes: ",
                                paste(unmapped, collapse = ", "))

  ## pull the matching within-vignette row for that participant + society
  dplyr::inner_join(long, pref, by = c(id, "condition_FutureSociety"))
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## Extract
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
L1_rows <- extractPreferredRows(level = 1)   # each participant's MOST preferred society
L2_rows <- extractPreferredRows(level = 2)   # each participant's 2nd preferred society

## quick checks
nrow(L1_rows)                                 # ~ one row per participant
count(L1_rows, condition_FutureSociety)       # how often each society is the L1 pick

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## L1 vs L2 in long form (for the AIS-adapted BI comparison / H2)
## -> one participant contributes two rows: pref_level L1 and L2.
## Run paired comparisons on the BI / AIS-adapted column(s) here.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
pref_L1L2 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(L1_rows, pref_level = "L1"),
  dplyr::mutate(L2_rows, pref_level = "L2")
) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(.data[[idCol]], pref_level)

head(pref_L1L2)
```



```{r}
## =====================================================================
## Join each participant's L1 (most-preferred society) row onto the wide
## between-person data -> H2 analysis frame.
## ques_study_wide already holds the AIS-adapted BI (aris_scale-ais1..4);
## L1_rows adds that society's pe (participative efficacy) + att (eval.).
## Requires: dplyr ; objects ques_study_wide and L1_rows in scope.
## =====================================================================
## one L1 row per participant?  (ties/missing ranks would break the 1:1 join)
if (anyDuplicated(L1_rows$PROLIFIC_PID))
  warning("L1_rows has >1 row for some PROLIFIC_PID -- the join will fan out.")

## prep L1 side: drop its ID (keep wide's), prefix the rest with "L1_",
## join key PROLIFIC_PID stays unprefixed.
L1_pref <- L1_rows %>%
  dplyr::select(-ID) %>%
  dplyr::rename_with(~ paste0("L1_", .x), .cols = -PROLIFIC_PID)

## attach to the wide frame (keep all 486 participants; NA where no L1 match)
ques_study_wide_L1 <- dplyr::left_join(ques_study_wide, L1_pref,
                                       by = "PROLIFIC_PID")

## checks
nrow(ques_study_wide_L1)                       # should stay 486
sum(is.na(ques_study_wide_L1$L1_condition_FutureSociety))  # unmatched participants
table(ques_study_wide_L1$L1_condition_FutureSociety, useNA = "ifany")

## now ready for H2, e.g. the AIS-adapted BI vs L1 evaluation:
##   ques_study_wide_L1$L1_mean_att   # desirability/attainability of L1 society
##   ques_study_wide_L1$L1_mean_pe    # participative efficacy for L1 society
##   ques_study_wide_L1[, c("aris_scale-ais1","aris_scale-ais2",
##                          "aris_scale-ais3","aris_scale-ais4")]  # BI items
```





```{r}
## =====================================================================
## H2 -- Evaluation -> motivation link (within individuals)
## Visions evaluated as more desirable/attainable should evoke higher
## participative efficacy (mean_pe) and stronger behavioural intentions
## (AIS-adapted BI).
## Vignette-level (long) data; the BI side is tested via the L1 setup.
## >>> RUN THIS AFTER the L1/L2 extraction + join chunks <<<
##     needs in scope: ques_study_within_vignettes, pref_L1L2,
##     ques_study_wide_L1  (the latter two come from those chunks).
## Requires: dplyr, lme4, lmerTest, psych, haven, writexl
## =====================================================================


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 0. Variable groups to keep
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
sampleVars <- c("age", "gender", "education", "employment_status",
                "lrscale", "rlgdgr")
rankVars   <- grep("^rank_",          colnames(ques_study_wide), value = TRUE)  # ranking task
biVars     <- grep("^aris_scale-ais", colnames(ques_study_wide), value = TRUE)  # AIS-adapted BI

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Build the H2 subset (long; evaluation + efficacy per vignette,
##    BI merged from wide, ranking + sample descriptors kept)
##    Evaluation = mean_att (composite); att_desirable = desirability item.
##    NOTE: there is no explicit "attainable" item among att_* (ideal,
##    beneficial, utopian, desirable, innovative, live_in) -- map your
##    intended attainability measure here if you have one.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
data_H2 <- ques_study_within_vignettes %>%
  dplyr::select(ID, PROLIFIC_PID, condition_FutureSociety, vignette_id,
                mean_att, sd_att, att_desirable, att_ideal,
                mean_pe, sd_pe) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    dplyr::select(ques_study_wide,
                  dplyr::all_of(c("PROLIFIC_PID", sampleVars, rankVars, biVars))),
    by = "PROLIFIC_PID")

## between-person AIS-adapted BI score (one value per person, repeated
## across that person's 7 vignette rows). No reverse items in AIS.
data_H2$mean_BI_AIS <- rowMeans(data_H2[biVars], na.rm = TRUE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Test H2
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## (a) WITHIN-person evaluation -> participative efficacy
##     mean_att varies across vignettes within a person.
m_eff <- lmer(mean_pe ~ mean_att + (1 | PROLIFIC_PID), data = data_H2)
summary(m_eff)
# optional random slope (if it converges):
# m_eff_rs <- lmer(mean_pe ~ mean_att + (1 + mean_att | PROLIFIC_PID), data = data_H2)

## (b) L1 vs L2 WITHIN-person contrast (evaluation/efficacy side):
##     the more-preferred vision (L1) should show higher pe / att than L2.
m_L1L2_pe  <- lmer(mean_pe  ~ pref_level + (1 | PROLIFIC_PID), data = pref_L1L2)
m_L1L2_att <- lmer(mean_att ~ pref_level + (1 | PROLIFIC_PID), data = pref_L1L2)
summary(m_L1L2_pe)
summary(m_L1L2_att)

## (c) BEHAVIOURAL INTENTIONS (AIS-adapted) are measured once per person,
##     so the att -> BI link is between-person. Tie BI to the evaluation of
##     each person's MOST-preferred (L1) society via the joined frame:
biVars_L1 <- grep("^aris_scale-ais", colnames(ques_study_wide_L1), value = TRUE)
ques_study_wide_L1$mean_BI_AIS <- rowMeans(ques_study_wide_L1[biVars_L1], na.rm = TRUE)

cor.test(ques_study_wide_L1$L1_mean_att, ques_study_wide_L1$mean_BI_AIS)
summary(lm(mean_BI_AIS ~ L1_mean_att + L1_mean_pe, data = ques_study_wide_L1))
## If BI was asked separately for L1 and L2, add those columns to
## pref_L1L2 and run a paired test there instead.

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Export the H2 subset: SPSS (.sav), Excel (.xlsx), R (.rds)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
exportDataset <- function(df, base, dir = ".") {
  if (!dir.exists(dir)) dir.create(dir, recursive = TRUE)
  clean <- df; names(clean) <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", names(clean))  # SPSS/Excel-safe names
  haven::write_sav(clean, file.path(dir, paste0(base, ".sav")))
  xl <- clean; f <- vapply(xl, is.factor, logical(1))
  xl[f] <- lapply(xl[f], as.character)
  writexl::write_xlsx(xl, file.path(dir, paste0(base, ".xlsx")))
  saveRDS(df, file.path(dir, paste0(base, ".rds")))
  invisible(NULL)
}

exportDataset(data_H2, "data_H2", OUTPUT_QUESTIONNAIRE_PIA_DIR)
```

```{r}
## =====================================================================
## H2 -- Evaluation -> motivation link (within individuals)
## Visions evaluated as more desirable/attainable should evoke higher
## participative efficacy (mean_pe) and stronger behavioural intentions
## (AIS-adapted BI).
## Vignette-level (long) data; the BI side is tested via the L1 setup.
## >>> RUN THIS AFTER the L1/L2 extraction + join chunks <<<
##     needs in scope: ques_study_within_vignettes, pref_L1L2,
##     ques_study_wide_L1  (the latter two come from those chunks).
## Requires: dplyr, lme4, lmerTest, psych, haven, writexl
## =====================================================================

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 0. Variable groups to keep
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
sampleVars <- c("age", "gender", "education", "employment_status",
                "lrscale", "rlgdgr")
rankVars   <- grep("^rank_",          colnames(ques_study_wide), value = TRUE)  # ranking task
biVars     <- grep("^aris_scale-ais", colnames(ques_study_wide), value = TRUE)  # AIS-adapted BI

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. H2 subset = each participant's PREFERRED (L1) society ONLY
##    L1 evaluation/efficacy (from L1_rows) + AIS-adapted activism
##    + ranking + sample descriptors  ->  ONE row per participant (486).
##    Evaluation = mean_att (composite); att_desirable = desirability item.
##    NOTE: no explicit "attainable" item among att_* (ideal, beneficial,
##    utopian, desirable, innovative, live_in) -- map yours here if you have one.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
data_H2 <- L1_rows %>%
  dplyr::select(ID, PROLIFIC_PID, condition_FutureSociety, vignette_id, pref_rank,
                mean_att, sd_att, att_desirable, att_ideal,
                mean_pe, sd_pe) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    dplyr::select(ques_study_wide,
                  dplyr::all_of(c("PROLIFIC_PID", sampleVars, rankVars, biVars))),
    by = "PROLIFIC_PID")

## AIS-adapted ACTIVISM intention (composite of the aris_scale-ais items;
## one value per person). No reverse items in AIS.
data_H2$mean_activism <- rowMeans(data_H2[biVars], na.rm = TRUE)
data_H2$sd_activism   <- apply(data_H2[biVars], 1L, sd, na.rm = TRUE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Test H2  (data_H2 is now one row per person -> between-person)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## (a) Evaluation of the PREFERRED society -> participative efficacy
cor.test(data_H2$mean_att, data_H2$mean_pe)

## (b) Evaluation / efficacy of the preferred society -> activism intentions
cor.test(data_H2$mean_att, data_H2$mean_activism)
summary(lm(mean_activism ~ mean_att + mean_pe, data = data_H2))

## (c) WITHIN-person check: L1 vs L2 contrast on evaluation/efficacy.
##     The more-preferred vision (L1) should show higher pe / att than L2.
##     (uses pref_L1L2, which carries two rows per person.)
m_L1L2_pe  <- lmer(mean_pe  ~ pref_level + (1 | PROLIFIC_PID), data = pref_L1L2)
m_L1L2_att <- lmer(mean_att ~ pref_level + (1 | PROLIFIC_PID), data = pref_L1L2)
summary(m_L1L2_pe)
summary(m_L1L2_att)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Export the H2 subset: SPSS (.sav), Excel (.xlsx), R (.rds)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
exportDataset <- function(df, base, dir = ".") {
  if (!dir.exists(dir)) dir.create(dir, recursive = TRUE)
  clean <- df; names(clean) <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", names(clean))  # SPSS/Excel-safe names
  haven::write_sav(clean, file.path(dir, paste0(base, ".sav")))
  xl <- clean; f <- vapply(xl, is.factor, logical(1))
  xl[f] <- lapply(xl[f], as.character)
  writexl::write_xlsx(xl, file.path(dir, paste0(base, ".xlsx")))
  saveRDS(df, file.path(dir, paste0(base, ".rds")))
  invisible(NULL)
}

exportDataset(data_H2, "data_H2", OUTPUT_QUESTIONNAIRE_PIA_DIR)
```
